threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think waiting for a bus means checking the timetable, not just standing there and hoping for the best.
Last night on the N63, a couple argued over a missing pie. Turns out it fell under the seat—had me in stitches as they searched for it!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I was home? Seeing a kid negotiate with a stray dog over the last piece of pizza on the street.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain do you find a techno club inside a former power plant, where dancing until dawn is accompanied by the sound of turbines.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell who's local when they ignore the BART delays and still complain about the heat in the subway. Tourists just look confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 with a guy serenading us with a ukulele. Two stops later, he was back to racing pigeons on the corner. Classic Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the local bars close early, but at 1am, you’ll find the real Gràcia nightlife just starting. The plaza is alive until dawn.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still ask for tap water at restaurants, not realizing it's a slow route to a bill surprise.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look puzzled when the bus driver closes the door before you sit down. Locals know to hop on quick or risk missing the ride.
Heard a bloke serenading the 59 with a ukulele last night, kept everyone unusually calm despite the delays. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found myself cheering on the kids at the Turkish soccer match in the park, realizing I knew half the players by name.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a park party that doubles as a protest against gentrification. Beats and banners coexist on Sundays in the canal park.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local by how they avoid eye contact at the BART because they know the real surprise is the train that's actually running on time.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full business suit on the 19 bus, sipping a latte while chatting up a saxophonist. Just another Tuesday morning in the 'loin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just for hipster bars, but many locals miss the small shops selling fresh herbs and spices hidden in quiet streets.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they’re new when they still squint at the Metro map; a local just knows the shortcuts through the maze of Passeig de Gràcia.
